I reviewed all four declarations in the file (lines 1–112): `directionalDerivative_mem_coefficientSubmodule`, `polynomialLogDerivative_mem_of_coefficients`, `polynomialDerivativeSystem_remove` and `polynomial_removal_preserves_derivative_layers`. I also read the lemmas they rely on: `dualLogDerivative_mem_of_invariant` (Linear/DualIdealSteps.lean), `dualDerivativeSystem_remove` and `derivative_removal_preserves_quotient_layers` (Linear/DualDerivativeRemoval.lean), `coefficients_directionalDerivative` (Estimates/ShiftedGradedCalculus.lean) and `eval_mem_iff_coefficients` (Polynomial/ExtendedPolynomialValues.lean).

No hypothesis set is inconsistent. For example, taking V = ⊥ (or V = ⊤), any LieSubalgebra U and A = C = 1 satisfies every assumption, so none of the statements hold only vacuously. Each conclusion is the expected polynomial version of the corresponding dual-number lemma, with the same shape. The base and tangent membership facts are obtained from coefficient hypotheses through `dualEvalLie_base` and `dualEvalLie_tangent`.

One thing I noted but did not report: `hAV` and `hCV` require every coefficient to lie in V, including the constant one (α = 0). By `coefficients_directionalDerivative`, the derivative only uses coefficients at `α + Finsupp.single i 1`, so the constant coefficient never affects the tangent part. The hypotheses are therefore stronger than the proofs need. However, they are still satisfiable. The file has no docstrings, and a search found no uses of these three theorems anywhere under `lean/`. With no stated purpose to compare against, calling this a misleading or vacuous statement would be speculation, so I left it out.

Remaining uncertainty: these lemmas have no downstream uses, so I could not check whether any intended application would actually need the weaker hypothesis.
